content: Iron rusts from disuse; stagnant water loses its purity; even so does inaction sap the vigor of the mind.
author: Leonardo da Vinci
sourceWork: Leonardo da Vinci's Essays & Philosophical Writings
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. Thinking about doing something gives us a comfortable dopamine hit of progress without any of the actual friction. We often use over-researching and planning as socially acceptable disguises for fear of starting.

In Leonardo da Vinci's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Clarity follows action; it does not precede it. You cannot think your way into a new way of living—you have to act your way into a new way of understanding. The smallest real-world step beats the most brilliant theory.
reflectionPrompt: How can you welcome mistakes and awkward beginnings as essential steps in your creative evolution?
